summary: Initial security intake with Ironbark to understand certification requirements and deployment constraints. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood CSM), Matt (CTO - Ironbark), Sofia (Head of Security), Ravi (Platform)

Summary (auto): quick security intake, clarify requirements for production inference with PII.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:05 Matt: Yup, loud and clear. thanks jordan.
00:09 Jordan: Awesome. So today we wanted to walk through Ironbark's security decision criteria — just basic intake. Priya will chime in on technical constraints and we'll call out hosting options.
00:20 Sofia: Great, we've got a short list: SOC2, ISO27001, SSO integration (Okta via SAML), customer keys, audit logs, and retention. Also curious about the hosted offering and whether we can route PII into Dedicated or Private.
00:35 Priya: Yep, that's totally reasonable. Quick clarifier — when you say PII, is that customer personally identifiable info in prompts, or PII in attachments/documents?
00:45 Ravi: Mostly prompt-level PII and some extracted PHI from our support transcripts. The real ask is that any PII used for inference must be under our KMS and logable in our SIEM.
00:58 Priya: Ok that helps. For Redwood we support three deployment modes — Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted is fastest to run but by default uses Redwood-managed keys unless you choose a BYOK flow with Dedicated/Private.
01:15 Sofia: Does Redwood offer customer-managed keys for Hosted?
01:20 Priya: Historically Hosted used Redwood-managed keys but we have a BYOK option for certain enterprise tiers; more commonly customers use Dedicated or Private for BYOK and HSM-backed keys. There's nuance with cross-region key residency too — we'll share the KMS doc.
01:36 Jordan: I'll send you the KMS integration doc with details on key wrapping and HSM compliance (FIPS 140-2/3 notes).
01:44 Matt: Perfect. On certifications — can you confirm scope of SOC2 and ISO? We need SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 scope covering the inference control plane and data flows.
01:58 Priya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO27001; I will attach the SOC2 report and an ISO readiness summary. Note that for Private deployments, customers can host the control plane in their own VPC which gives additional scope control.
02:12 Sofia: Good — also need to understand penetration testing cadence, 3rd-party attestations, and whether Redwood provides a vulnerability management feed we can ingest.
02:23 Evan: We do regular pentests annually and can provide a summary of findings and remediations. We also publish a vulnerability disclosure program and CVE tracking. For enterprise customers we can coordinate an NDA'd questionnaire.
02:37 Ravi: Ok. Audit logs — we need request-level audit logs (who called what model, request id, tokenized counts, timestamps) and the ability to stream logs to our Splunk instance. What's the retention and granularity?
02:52 Priya: We surface per-request traces and logs in the Console; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and direct log sinks to SIEMs via secure syslog or Kinesis. For Hosted, longer retention is possible as an add-on but default retention is limited for privacy. We'll provide the log schema.
03:10 Sofia: And SSO? We use Okta — SAML + SCIM provisioning. How mature is Redwood's SAML and SCIM support?
03:19 Priya: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based in Console with built-in roles and custom roles for least-privilege. We also support session length and RBAC audits.
03:34 Matt: Do you support JIT provisioning? We prefer SCIM plus attribute mapping so roles can be mapped from our directory.
03:43 Priya: Yes SCIM supports attribute mappings. There are a few gotchas around group nesting — we'll share a SCIM mapping example for Okta.
03:52 Sofia: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain datasets. Can we guarantee that inference for particular routes stays in eu-west-1?
04:02 Priya: Yes, Smart routing lets you pin model endpoints to regions and we can set policies per-route. For Hosted customers you can choose region; Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees and network isolation.
04:16 Ravi: What about data deletion? If a user requests deletion do you purge prompt logs and cache entries? We need proof of deletion procedures.
04:25 Jordan: We have deletion APIs and documented retention policies. For Dedicated/Private you can implement controlled retention windows at the cluster level. For Hosted we will coordinate a data deletion ticket and provide attestations.
04:38 Sofia: Any limitations on KV cache or prefix caching that might leave residuals?
04:45 Priya: KV caches are per-inference session and can be configured for TTLs; for sensitive workloads we'd recommend disabling prefix caching or using Private so you control storage.
04:55 Matt: About encryption in transit — TLS is standard but do you support mutual TLS for backend-to-backend?
05:03 Priya: We support mTLS for private peering and for Dedicated/private network endpoints. Hosted public endpoints use TLS 1.2/1.3.
05:13 Ravi: And key rotation? If we BYOK, can we rotate keys without downtime?
05:18 Priya: With KMS-backed key wrapping you can rotate keys; there's a short cutover window but no planned downtime — we handle key wrapping version negotiation in the runtime. We'll document the rotation procedure.
05:31 Sofia: SIEM integration — we want to stream logs and also have alerting for anomalous calls. Any built-in anomaly detection?
05:40 Evan: We provide basic usage anomaly alerts and you can export logs to SIEM for correlation. Advanced behavioral detection we recommend running in your SIEM against the exported logs.
05:50 Matt: What's the onboarding timeline if we choose Dedicated vs Private? We need to present to leadership by mid-Jan '28.
05:57 Jordan: For Dedicated you can be up in 4–6 weeks after contract — capacity provisioning and networking. Private (VPC or on-prem) typically 8–12 weeks depending on approvals and on-prem constraints. That aligns with a Jan go/no-go.
06:10 Sofia: For procurement we will need pricing for hosted with high-retention add-on, and for a 3-node Dedicated baseline with BYOK. Also SLA details.
06:20 Jordan: We'll include pricing options and the Dedicated sizing baseline.
06:23 Ravi: One more technical — latency SLAs for 4k token sessions? We need p50/p95 numbers and whether batching impacts tail latency.
06:32 Priya: We'll run a 2-hour benchmark with your typical sequence lengths; batching improves throughput but can increase p95. We'll share previous profiles and run the test on a Dedicated replica to show typical p50/p95.
06:45 Sofia: Any compliance add-ons around audit log immutability or WORM storage?
06:50 Priya: For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with WORM buckets and append-only log sinks. Hosted can be configured with extended retention but immutability usually requires customer-managed storage.
07:03 Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send SOC2 and the KMS/HSM doc; Priya will provision a sandbox and schedule perf runs; Ravi will share KMS diagram and retention windows.
07:16 Matt: Sounds good. If we get the SOC2 and KMS docs we can prep a short internal risk memo.
07:22 Sofia: Also add an appendix that lists required artifacts for procurement and security approvals.
07:27 Jordan: Will do — I'll attach the list and also a checklist for Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.
07:33 Evan: We'll be available for a narrower technical deep dive on key wrapping if needed.
07:38 Matt: Thank you all.
07:40 Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the perf run.
07:45 Call ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional dropped words, proper nouns sometimes garbled (e.g., 'Redwood Optima' instead of 'Redwood Optimize'), speaker labels approximate.
